episode.title: How Britain Won History's Shortest War In 1896!

synopsis: The Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896 ended in under forty-five minutes when naval gunfire crippled the royal palace.
narration: In 1896, the shortest war in recorded history broke out and concluded in under forty-five minutes. British Royal Navy warships bombarded the royal palace of Zanzibar until the sultan fled, ending the conflict almost immediately.

shots.prompt: In 9:16 vertical view, smoke billows over the ornate waterfront palace of Zanzibar in 1896 as naval artillery shells burst in mid-air above decorated coral-stone balconies. Dense grey haze drifts fast across sunlit turquoise sea while British armored cruisers fire from the harbor, sparks snapping off carved wooden doors.

A tight, dramatic close-up of a brass marine clock on a warship deck ticking rapidly past thirty-eight minutes, its glass face reflecting lingering smoke plumes and the royal banner sliding down a scorched flagpole in the background, framing a silent, still resolve.

music: Fast, tense, percussive underscore driven by rapid brass hits, aggressive snare rolls, and heavy wooden percussion. The arrangement opens instantly at full speed, maintaining unrelenting rhythmic pressure with dramatic low-register orchestral swells, ending abruptly mid-beat to allow seamless video looping.
